clue.text: Mount leading horse

parts.note: the leading competitor is the best one
a jockey calls the horse they are riding in a race their ride

explanation.surface: An instruction to climb onto the front horse in a string.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride something is to sit astride it, as a rider sits on a horse, so a verb meaning to get up on.

clue.text: Confuse or inspire artist?

definitions.meaning: a muse is the figure who inspires a painter or poet, so to inspire one is to be their muse; the question mark flags the split phrase

explanation.surface: Asks whether something baffles a painter or fires their imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewildering someone is a plain synonym; the second sense splits the word into a two-word phrase about acting as an artist's inspiration.

clue.text: Vegetable is unfashionable following first half of growing season

indicators.note: the word for unfashionable comes after the cut-down season
only the opening half of the season's name is kept, its first three of six letters

parts.note: spring is the season when plants start to grow
something unfashionable is out

explanation.surface: A vegetable that has gone out of style just as the growing season gets under way.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brussels sprout is a familiar green vegetable, especially at Christmas in Britain.

clue.text: Leave job sacrificing second period in charge

indicators.note: giving something up, so the abbreviation for second is dropped from the word for quitting

parts.note: to leave a job formally is to resign

explanation.surface: Someone quits a post, giving up their deputy, during a spell of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the stretch of time during which they rule.

clue.text: Attracting doctor inspiring dread

parts.note: awing means filling someone with awe, a mixture of dread and wonder

explanation.surface: A frightening doctor who still pulls people in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like an insertion signal, but 'inspiring dread' is a single synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a crowd is to attract it, so drawing is a synonym of attracting.

clue.text: Undergarments in galleria on board ship

indicators.note: something on board a ship is inside it, so the shopping word sits between the two letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a galleria is a shopping arcade, a mall

explanation.surface: Underwear on sale in a shopping arcade aboard a cruise ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Smalls is British informal for underwear, the small items in a wash.

clue.text: In Barcelona Mary embraces John in grass

indicators.note: the Spanish form of Mary holds the Spanish John within it

parts.note: Maria is the Spanish form of Mary
Juan is John in Spanish, still governed by 'In Barcelona'

explanation.surface: A Spanish couple share a romantic moment lying in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Barcelona' applies to both names. Maria is split after its I so that Juan fits before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is a long-standing slang name for cannabis.

clue.text: Idly swimming in pool that's refined

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for pool

parts.note: a lake is a large pool of water

indicators.note: the letters of idly are moving about as if swimming

explanation.surface: Someone lazily swimming in an elegant pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges IDLY to DYLI, which goes into LAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladylike describes polished, genteel behaviour, so refined is a synonym.

clue.text: Wantonly depletes appearance of some churches

definitions.note: the definition describes how some churches look, an adjective sense: having spires

indicators.note: acting wantonly is acting without restraint, so the letters of depletes are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone recklessly drains away the look of certain churches.
explanation.definitionFit: A church with a tall spired tower is described as having that look; many village churches have spires.

clue.text: Drive back fly on a new form of confectionery

indicators.note: the word for drive is read backwards

parts.note: to drive a stake in is to ram it
a trouser fly is fastened with a zip

explanation.surface: Someone drives an insect away from a new kind of sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like an insect; here it is the fastening on trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Marzipan is an almond paste sweet used on cakes and moulded into shapes.

clue.text: Bottom of egg fried badly in kitchen appliance

indicators.note: done badly, so the letters come out jumbled
the bottom of a word is its final letter, here of egg

explanation.surface: The underside of an egg was overcooked in some kitchen gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges FRIED together with G into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fridge, short for refrigerator, is a standard appliance for keeping food cold.

clue.text: Regularly engages spurs

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Someone often hires riding spurs, or keeps engaging and encouraging.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge them forward, just as spurring them does.

clue.text: Looking sideways at one of five children wearing fleece

indicators.note: the child is inside the word for fleece, as if dressed in it

parts.note: to fleece someone is to cheat them, and a sting is a confidence trick
a quin is one of quintuplets, five born together

explanation.surface: Peering askance at one of quintuplets dressed in a woolly fleece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like a garment, which 'wearing' encourages; it is the swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Squinting can mean glancing obliquely or out of the side of the eyes, so looking askance.

clue.text: Drink in short pitcher starts to loosen everyone's principles

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the vessel word is lost

parts.note: a pitcher is a jug

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A drink kept in a little pitcher begins to relax everybody's morals.
explanation.definitionFit: A julep is a sweet drink, best known as the mint julep of the American South.

clue.text: Try to get silver coating on edge of seat

indicators.note: the chemical symbol for silver wraps round the other word like a coating

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver, from Latin argentum
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: An attempt to silver-plate the edge of a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agog means eagerly excited, the state of a spectator leaning forward on the edge of their seat.

clue.text: Dog worrying young herd

indicators.note: worrying is what a dog does to sheep, harassing them, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A dog harassing a flock of young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A greyhound is a slender breed of dog used for racing.

clue.text: Around a thousand scattered pearls glisten

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the symbol for a thousand
the pearls are scattered, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: K is short for kilo, a thousand

explanation.surface: About a thousand loose pearls shimmering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges PEARLS, and 'Around' puts that round K.
explanation.definitionFit: To sparkle is to shine with flashes of light, much as things glisten.

clue.text: Father left Eastern axes after a major fit

indicators.note: the father, left, eastern and axes pieces come after the A

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
x and y are the two axes of a graph

explanation.surface: Dad leaves oriental axes after a big tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplexy is a stroke, a seizure, or by extension a fit of rage.

clue.text: Put off upright individual holding power

indicators.note: the pair of words for upright and individual hold the power symbol between them

parts.note: a post is an upright pole
one is a single individual
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A stiff, formal person who clings to power delays things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright' and 'individual' look like a description of one person, but they are two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off a meeting is to delay it to a later time, the synonym's meaning.

clue.text: Saw rambler in empty bar

indicators.note: the wanderer goes inside the emptied drinking place
emptied of its contents, so the middle letter of the drinking place goes

parts.note: a pub is a bar
a rover is someone who rambles or wanders

explanation.surface: A walker found in a bar with no customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense or a tool; it is an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying or maxim, so a synonym of an adage like this.

clue.text: Worthless American fellow generating junk mail?

parts.note: bum is American slang meaning worthless or poor-quality

explanation.surface: A useless American man produces unwanted post.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is British slang for useless paperwork and printed matter, such as unsolicited circulars; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Max talks endlessly

indicators.note: without its ends, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: speaks is a synonym of talks

explanation.surface: Someone named Max who never stops chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Max' looks like a man's name; it is short for maximum.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is the highest point, so the maximum level of something.

clue.text: Sweet dog swallowing date and half of meal

indicators.note: the dog breed's name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

indicators.note: the first half of the word for meal is kept

parts.note: dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: A dog wolfing down a date and part of its dinner, for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudding is the British word for dessert, the sweet course of a meal.

clue.text: Unpleasantly inhabit bargain festival clothes

indicators.note: a verb: the outer words clothe the answer, which sits inside them

explanation.surface: Cheap festival outfits that are crawling with bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun; it is a verb meaning covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pests that infest a place live there in large, troublesome numbers.

clue.text: Exclusive clubs fail to degree

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
to lose is to fail

explanation.surface: Members-only clubs fail to some extent.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed group admits no outsiders, so it is exclusive.

clue.text: Shy salesman's patter

definitions.meaning: a sales ..., the spiel a salesperson gives

explanation.surface: A timid seller's chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy, matching a throw; and a sales spiel is a well-known phrase.

clue.text: Healing mild acne I developed

indicators.note: the letters develop into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A patient says their mild acne got worse while being treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicinal means having the power to cure, so an adjective close to healing.

clue.text: Snuck salesman into court

indicators.note: the salesman goes inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A salesperson sneaked into a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Snuck is an informal past tense of sneak; to creep is to move stealthily, so a synonym.

clue.text: Book flight

definitions.meaning: the second book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Reserve an aeroplane seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The second book of the Old Testament, and also a mass departure of people fleeing a place.

clue.text: Sentence the French said initially for dead

parts.note: a life sentence is a prison term
les is French for the (plural)

indicators.note: taking the first letter of said

explanation.surface: A judge pronounces a sentence in French on someone already gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifeless has no life in it, as a corpse has none.

clue.text: Taking exercise speedily produces returns

indicators.note: taking away the abbreviation for exercise from the pool of letters
the letters of speedily, rearranged, produce the answer with something left over

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Working out at speed brings profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produces' rearranges SPEEDILY; 'Taking' removes PE, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yields as a noun plural are the returns on an investment.

clue.text: Excited when bit of Italianate bric-a-brac is found in old container

indicators.note: the pieces turn up inside the word for old

parts.note: aged is old

indicators.note: a bit of the word here means its first letter

parts.note: tat is cheap, worthless ornaments or junk

explanation.surface: Thrilled at finding Italian-style trinkets inside an antique box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container' just reinforces that AGED holds the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be agitated is to be stirred up or worked up, a near-synonym of excited.
